### F-278 · ambiguity · timing.v1 §2.7, §5: how long a tool held a known member whose wait its owner's absence stopped

> §2.7: "For each member it holds, the tool has: how long it held the
> member in the window: from the later of the window's start and the
> instant it first held it (its first arrival, or, for a known member, the
> instant it began to wait for it) to the window's end, or to the member's
> end".

> §2.5: "If its owner is absent before the miss is due, a member waited
> for from its owner's presence waits for nothing until the owner is
> present again, and counts from then", and "A known member is never
> forgotten". `deadlines.json`'s description: "owner absent: without
> epoch, every waited-for member is no longer waited for", the member
> still held.

> §5, the deadline's Yes: "No miss reported in the window, and the member
> held for longer than the deadline in it (`met`)"; its Unobservable:
> "held for the deadline or less (`window_too_short`)".

Take a known member never heard whose owner is present at the window's
start and shown absent by a complete read before its miss is due. Its
wait stops, so no miss is reported, and nothing ends it. By §2.7 as
written it is held from the window's start to the window's end, and §5
answers its deadline **yes, `met`**: a pass from a window that waited for
it for less than its deadline, and in which nothing arrived.

The two tools read it apart (`timing_interop --only gone`, beside §6, not
a scenario). `pace.v1`'s `cmd` was never published. The owner, present at
the window's start, closed cleanly 0.15 s into a 3 s window, before `cmd`'s
miss was due at 0.5 s. With either owner, in every run:
- **zk2py's tool**, by the text: `cmd` held 3,000 ms, its deadline **yes,
  `met`**, and so the resource's and the run's;
- **`zenctl timing`**: `held_ms` 328–369 ms, from the window's start to the
  read that showed the owner absent, and its deadline **unobservable,
  `window_too_short`**.

Both read `cmd`'s period unobservable (`owner_not_present`: no arrival
over a 3 s span) and its lifespan unobservable (`no_sample`), so with
`pace.v1` both runs exit 2. The run's exit moves with a copy of `pace.v1`
whose `cmd` declares a deadline alone, served by zk2py's owner (a probe of
this round's, run once, not kept in the runner: the reference's owner
serves `pace.v1` alone): zk2py's tool exits 0, every question asked clean
(the deadline `met`, the period and the lifespan not asked), and `zenctl
timing` exits 2, its `held_ms` 328 ms.

It changes a verdict: a member's deadline, `yes` against `unobservable`,
and a run's exit. It needs a test too. `conclusions.json` takes `held_ms`
as its input, and `deadlines.json`, which turns events into the tracker's
account, reports no held time, so no fixture says how long such a member
was held. zk2py follows the text, and its check prints XFAIL. Wording
that would settle it, either way:
- "…; for a known member never heard, only while it waited for it (§2.5):
  its owner's absence stops the count, and its presence again starts it",
  the reference's reading, with a scenario step (§6: `cmd` never
  published, the owner closing 0.15 s in: deadline unobservable,
  `window_too_short`) or `deadlines.json` reporting each member's held
  time; or
- the text as it stands, with that step's `met`, and the reference's tool
  fixed to it.

zk2py prefers the first: a pass the window could not have failed is the
vacuous `met` that `window_too_short` exists to refuse.

### F-279 · wording · timing.v1 §5: a roll-up's reason

> §5: "The fixture `conclusions.json` states the tokens: `yes`, `no`,
> `unobservable`, `not_asked`, `not_this_profiles`, each with a reason".

> `conclusions.json`'s description, of a roll-up: "expect.answer is, read
> by the question's finding …", the answer alone.

§5 states how a resource's or a run's answer is read, never its reason,
and no roll-up case gives one. Both tools print one: the reason of the
first member giving the answer (zenctl's `first`; zk2py's first in its
rows' order, the canonical form's resources, then each one's members by
key). In every step of §6 and §2.8 the two agree. Over no member at all
they differ:
- zk2py writes `unobservable`, `no_member`, a reason of its own making;
- `zenctl timing` writes `unobservable` with no `reason` field and
  `members: {}`.

`timing_interop --only gone` shows it on `axis/{axis}`, no axis published,
as a separate check (XFAIL). Which member is "first" is unstated as well,
so over members that give one answer with two reasons the tools could
name different ones. No scenario makes that, and zk2py did not.

It changes no verdict and no exit. It is wording only: "a roll-up's reason
is the first such member's, in member order (byte order of the keys);
over no member, none", or a word that says the reason is the tool's. zk2py
would then print none over no member.

### F-280 · ambiguity · timing.v1 §2.7: a member that ends in the window and is heard again

> §2.5: "A member heard after it ended is judged from that arrival, as a
> member first heard".

> §2.7: "**the span** runs from the window's start for a known member, else
> from the member's first arrival in the window, to the window's end, or to
> the member's end when it ended in the window"; the deadline's held time,
> likewise, runs "to the window's end, or to the member's end".

> `conclusions.json`: "ended, whether the member ended in the window",
> read after the misses and before `held_ms`: "ended: not_asked, ended".

§2.7 reads one life of a member per window. A member that ends in the
window and is heard again has two. The text says neither which end is "the
member's end", nor whether the second life is judged.

Both tools ran beside each owner (`timing_interop --only again`, beside §6,
not a scenario). `axis/x`'s member token was withdrawn 1 s into a 5 s
window (`timing remove x`), so each tool ended it, `gone`, at its read:
1.10–1.11 s in for zk2py, 1.18–1.23 s for zenctl. It was added again 2 s
in (`timing add x`) and heard every 100 ms to the window's end.
- **zk2py's tool, as round 80 first ran it,** dropped an end that an
  arrival followed. The span ran to the window's end, and the 1 s the
  member did not exist counted against it: 39 to 40 arrivals over 4.9 s,
  period **no, `not_kept`**, the owner present throughout. The run exited
  1.
- **`zenctl timing`** ended the span at the first end (`span_ms`
  1,118–1,152): period **yes, `kept`**, and the run exited 0.

zk2py now reads "the member's end" as its first end, as the letter reads.
`readings` holds the case: kept to the first end, not kept to the
window's end. The two tools now agree on every answer and exit, in both
runs. Their held times still differ, though no answer here reads them
(`ended` comes first): zk2py's 1,028–1,072 ms runs to the first end, and
zenctl's 3,940–4,054 ms sums both lives.

Neither tool now judges the second life's period, 3 s of arrivals that
could keep it or not. A miss in that life would still be reported, since
the misses are read before `ended`.

It changes a verdict: zk2py's first reading moved the run's exit. It
needs a test too: no fixture has a member that ends and comes back.
Wording that would settle it, either way:
- "a member that ends in the window and is heard again is read over its
  first life alone: the span and the held time end at its first end", as
  both tools now read the span; or
- each life a span of its own, the period's finding when any life's is,
  and the held time their sum, the reference's held time.

- **A re-mint and "present throughout".** §0's "present while the reader
  holds that token" reads, with "held by an instance of the member's
  provider address", as any instance's token, so a make-before-break
  re-mint keeps the owner present. zk2py's view reads it so, at the
  address.
- **When the read after a member token's withdrawal comes.** zenctl ended
  `axis/x` 180–230 ms after its withdrawal, and zk2py 107–112 ms after,
  each well before the 500 ms due. No verdict moves.

**After review-bot on PR #939.** Nothing blocking; its should-fixes and
nits are made.
- **An end before the member was first held** ends nothing.
  `zk2py.timing.window_held` holds a member from the later of the window's
  start and the instant it first held it, to the first end at or after
  that instant, else to the window's end. An earlier end can no longer
  give a held time of 0, nor `ended`, and so neither `window_too_short`
  nor `not_asked` wrongly. `Window._reading` uses it. A `readings` case
  pins it: an end at 100 ms of a member first held at 200 ms ends nothing
  (held 2,800 of 3,000 ms), and one at 1.5 s ends it there.
- **The tool sections run** (§6, `face`, `gone`, `again`) beside each owner
  the selected pairs name, and only with both tools present. A crash is
  reported under the section's own name.
- **`again`'s margins are wide.** The window is now 8 s, the withdrawal
  2 s in and the re-add 4 s in, so each life is 2 s or more against the
  windows' 72–113 ms start skew. The checks of each tool alone are what
  the text fixes: ended (`gone`), no miss, the deadline `not_asked`
  (`ended`), the lifespan not asked. The period kept over the first life
  is F-280's reading, checked once over both tools.
- **Nits.** The tool documents are read with `.get` throughout, so a
  malformed one fails a check rather than aborting a section. In
  `rollup`'s every-member-set-aside branch, `next` has a default and an
  assert.

### F-278 to F-280 at 0.5: resolved

**F-278, resolved.**

> §2.7 (0.5): "how long it held the member in the window: the **longest
> stretch** it held it without a pause, never the sum of its stretches …
> A pause is the owner's absence stopping a wait: a known member never
> heard is held only while it is waited for (§2.5), so its owner's
> absence stops the stretch, and its presence again starts a new one."

It is resolved as round 80 preferred, the reference's reading: a known
member never heard whose owner is read absent before its miss is due is
held only while it was waited for, and §5 answers its deadline
`window_too_short`, never `met`. The ruling beside it, the longest stretch
and never the sum, closes the same vacuous pass for an owner that comes
and goes. `deadlines.json` #46, #47 and #51 and `conclusions.json` #50 pin
it, and scenarios §6 step 5 runs it. zk2py's tool held `cmd` 160–185 ms in
step 5 (zenctl 254 ms) and 253–259 ms in round 80's `gone` (zenctl
317–340 ms), and both answered `window_too_short`.

**F-279, resolved.**

> §5 (0.5): "**A roll-up's reason** (text 0.5, F-279) is the reason of
> the first member giving its answer, in byte order of the members' keys
> … Over no member there is none."

It is the wording round 80 proposed, and `conclusions.json` #43 to #49
give each member's key and reason and state the roll-up's. zk2py's
`rollup` now orders `(key, answer)` pairs by their keys' bytes, and over no
member gives no reason, where round 80 printed `no_member`. Both tools'
roll-ups over the axis resource with no member read `unobservable` with no
reason, and every resource's and run's reason agreed at every step and
window.

**F-280, resolved.**

> §2.7 (0.5): "A member that ended in the window and is heard again in
> it, judged from that arrival as a member first heard (§2.5), is read
> over its **first life**: its span and its held time end at its first
> end, and its second life's period is not judged."

It is round 80's first wording. `periods.json` #21 (kept over the first
life, not kept to the window's end) and `deadlines.json` #48 (held 1,050 ms
of the first life, the second life's miss reported) pin it, and §6 step 6
runs it. The two tools' held times now agree on the life they count:
`axis/x` held 1,003–1,021 ms by zk2py and 1,104–1,123 ms by zenctl in step
6, and 2,021–2,036 ms against 2,123–2,138 ms in `again`, where round 80's
zenctl summed both lives (5,933–6,037 ms). Each tool's span equalled its
held time.

### timing.v1 0.5 in zk2py

- **`zk2py.timing`:**
  - the `Tracker` takes an `end` event, a tool's window closing, and keeps
    each member's held time: its longest unbroken stretch, a stretch
    running while it holds the member heard, missed or waited for
    (`deadlines.json`'s description), so a known member never heard
    pauses at its owner's absence and starts a new stretch at its presence
    again, and the member's first `ended` stops it for good (`held_ns`,
    `first_end`, `held_in_window`);
  - `rollup` takes `(key, Answer)` pairs, reads its reason from the first
    member giving its answer in byte order of the keys, and gives none over
    no member; `Answer.reason` may be `None`.
- **The runner:** `deadlines.json`'s `end` and `expect.held_ms`, and
  `conclusions.json`'s `rollup.members` and `expect.reason`. The first
  `rollup.members` case crashed the family until it read them; then all
  fifteen new cases passed the first time they ran, `periods.json` #21
  with no change. `timing` 196 of 196.
- **`zk2py.timing_live`:** the `Window` ends each tracker's window at its
  end and reads each member's held time and first end from the tracker; a
  resource holding no tracker (no deadline judged) keeps
  `window_held`, which no answer reads. Only samples within the window
  are judged for the lifespan.
- **`zk2py.timing_tool`:** each roll-up gives its `reason` and `first`
  only when there is a member, as `zenctl timing` does; a member row gives
  its `span_ms`, its first end as `ended`, and its arrivals within the
  window.
- **`readings`:** 518 (516 before). F-278's and F-280's readings went, the
  fixtures holding them now; four of 0.5 are new: a missed member held
  through its owner's absence, a paused member heard while its owner is
  absent (a new stretch), a member ended and not heard again keeping its
  held time, and a run's reason in byte order over pairs handed in row
  order. F-277's reading reads no reason over no member.
- **`zk2py.timing_scenarios`:** §6 steps 5 and 6, both passing.
- **`just py-conformance`: 3472 of 3472.**

**The windows beside §6** (round 81, both tools, both owners, both runs),

- **`waits`:** `cmd` waited for three times in a 4 s window, its owner

  more; both tools held the longest, 302–311 ms, and answered
  `window_too_short`, exit 2.

  closing 1 s in. §2.5's pause is the owner's absence "before the miss is
  due", so none here: both tools held it to the window's end, 3,000–3,002
  ms, and answered `no`, `missed`, exit 1.
- **`stray`:** `cmd` paused at its owner's absence 0.15 s in, then heard
  from 1 s every 100 ms on a raw session's puts while its owner is absent.
  Heard, it is held from that arrival: both tools held it 1,918–1,999 ms
  (zenctl's less by its earlier start), answered its deadline `yes`,
  `met`, its period `owner_not_present` and its lifespan `foreign_stamp`,
  exit 2.

### Not findings

- **A missed member and its owner's absence.** §2.7's "a known member never
  heard is held only while it is waited for" could be read to pause a
  member missed before its owner left. §2.5's pause is the owner's absence
  "before the miss is due", and `deadlines.json`'s description holds the
  member "heard, missed or waited for", as the CHANGELOG's "A missed member
  counts held while it stays missed" says. Both tools held `missed`'s
  `cmd` to the window's end, and §5 reads the misses first, so no answer
  could move.
- **A paused member heard again.** v1.md names only "its presence again"
  as starting a new stretch, but a stretch "begins at … the instant the
  tool held the member (its first arrival …)", and the description's
  "heard, missed or waited for" holds a member heard while its owner is
  absent. Both tools held `stray`'s `cmd` from that arrival. The
  CHANGELOG's "A heard member counts held from the instant it was first
  held … to the window's end … whatever presence says after it" would, by
  its letter, count `stray`'s from its first wait, 3,000 ms; it describes
  the common case, and v1.md's longest stretch bounds it. Both read `met`.
- **A known epoch member that ends unheard.** `deadlines.json`'s "its first
  ended stops it for good" names the report, which §2.5 makes only for a
  member heard or missed. A known member of an epoch template, waited for
  and never heard, whose token goes, ends with no report, and the
  description would hold its next wait as a new stretch. No case has one,
  and no tool can hold one: a tool knows only a template with no
  parameter (§2.7), and `epoch` names a parameter (core §2.3). A
  consumer's held time is read by no answer.
- **Which members `held_ms` names.** "each member the tracker held in the
  window" is any member held at any instant of it, as §2.7's "each member
  it held in a window, at any instant of it" reads (F-267). No case has a
  member held in the window and not held at its end; zk2py's `readings`
  holds one, its time kept.
- **The CHANGELOG's case list.** "#46 to #50" lists four cases; #48 is
  F-280's, named in its own bullet. The fixture holds six, #51 the two
  waits'.

**After review-bot on PR #941.** Nothing blocking; its three
should-fixes are made, and its nit.
- **One member set.** The `Window` holds `readings` and `spans` from its
  start, fills both in `end` over the members it answers, and asserts the
  three key sets equal; `zk2py.timing_tool` indexes them, so a member
  missing from either fails rather than printing `span_ms` null.
- **`Tracker.end` is single-use:** a second call judges nothing and adds no
  report, and the window's end and held times stay as the first left
  them. A `readings` case pins it.
- **The roll-up's two forms are explicit.** `rollup` takes `(key, Answer)`
  pairs alone, read in byte order of the keys for its reason, and
  `rollup_answer` answer tokens alone, for `conclusions.json`'s
  `rollup.answers`, where no reason is read; each raises `TypeError` on the
  other's form or a mix. Every caller that reads a reason passes pairs.
  A `readings` case pins both refusals.
- **The nit:** each live check's held-time range says what it must tell
  apart (for instance §6 step 6's 800–1,400 ms: the first life against
  both lives summed, about 4 s, and a span to the window's end, about
  5 s), beside `PLACE_MS`'s.

After them, `just py-conformance` passes 3474 of 3474 (`readings` 520),
and §6's six steps and the six windows beside it, both tools beside both
owners, 106 of 106.

## At core 0.58 and observer.md 0.1 (#925, #937)

Round 82 read core 0.57 and 0.58 and `spec/observer.md` text 0.1 cold, on
main 4fc62c69 (PR #948). It checked that the move of the reader's
discipline lost nothing that zk2py implements, read every MUST and SHOULD
of `observer.md` against its evidence, implemented core 0.57's
`cardinality = "unbounded"` and what `observer.md` asks that zk2py did
not yet do, and ran the live runners that exercise the reader's rules.
The reference's parties and tool ran as black boxes (`owner`, `consume`,
`zk2` and `zenctl` in `/srv/dev/targets/zenkey-tier/blackbox/`, built
2026-10-29 23:36, their `--help` read, their source never). It read, as
a newcomer would:
- `spec/observer.md` 0.1 whole, and `observer-CHANGELOG.md`;
- `spec/CHANGELOG.md`'s 0.57 and 0.58 entries, and every line core 0.58
  changed, every pointer it left among them;
- `profiles/README.md`'s new index and process, and the `experimental`
  entries of `timing.v1` and `arbitration.v1`;
- the two new contract fixtures, `contract.schema.json`'s `Cardinality`
  and `examples/zk2/README.md`'s draft 2.

Since round 81, `spec/` and `examples/zk2/` changed in ten commits,
e98622ea, 4573f359, 03e69019, 7d474584, ff0d6959 (`contract.schema.json`),
c7539263 (core 0.57), c2c61273 (draft 2), 09c5930a (core 0.58 and
`observer.md`), 3436a6ae (the changelogs) and 0db0621b (a link). zk2py
read their `spec/` and `examples/zk2/` files alone. No profile text's
version moved.

### What the move must not lose

**Mechanically.** The 713 lines core 0.58 removed from 0.57 were split into
sentences and normalized for the move's one licensed change, references
(a `core ` prefix, a § number, a link, `Appendix B`). Every sentence of
more than 25 characters stands in `observer.md` 0.1 or still in core
0.58. The eighteen that matched neither were each read: hunks the diff
spliced together (a line the move removed beside one it kept), and the
subjects §0 says a bullet names where only a sentence moved ("comparing
the stamp's id with it" became "with the owner's `meta.zid`"; §7.1's
"Generic tools" column became §7.3's bullet). The other way, every
sentence of observer §3 to §7 not in core 0.57 is a heading, a "Moved
from … stay in core §n" line, one of those bullets, a reference
rewritten, or one of the two restatements the changelog declares (§4.2's
admin space off by default, §6.1's opening). No rule was lost, and none
changed.

**Evidence, citation by citation.** Each `[F:]` and `[Sc:]` core 0.58
removed stands in `observer.md` or in a core line 0.58 rewrote, as often
as it was removed, but for one change: observer §7.2, a tool judging O3
from outside, cites `[Sc: operations.md §3, §5]`, where 0.57's block
shared `[Sc: operations.md §2, §3, §6]` with the owner's half (F-284).

blocks that moved, with its new home:

### F-291 · contradiction · observer 0.2 §1, "Not this profile's": kept apart from NotAsked, where three profiles report it as not asked

> §1 (text 0.2, F-286): "That answer is Unestablished, a kind of its own:
> kept apart from NotAsked and from Unobservable in every medium, as they
> are kept apart from each other, and never Established(no) … The
> profiles' fixtures give it as the token `not_this_profiles`."

- **Three profiles give the token,** as §1 cites: `timing.v1`,
  `arbitration.v1` and `redundancy.v1`, each in its `conclusions.json`.
- **Three others name a "not this profile's" answer, and report it as not
  asked:**
  - **`freshness.v1` §5:** "A premise that does not hold is reported
    `not_asked`, with the reason `kind` or `deleted`". `judgements.json`'s
    "an event: not this profile's (§2.2)" and "an operation: …" expect
    `{"verdict": "not_asked", "reason": "kind"}`, and §2.7 combines "not
    asked, or not this profile's" as one answer.
  - **`telemetry.v1` §5:** "'Not asked' (nobody put the question, or its
    premise does not hold)". Its sample's row reads "**Not asked:**
    `not_this_profiles`, `ignored`". `samples.json`'s "a composite state:
    not this profile's" expects conformance `not_asked`, reasons
    `["not_this_profiles"]`. Its declaration's `not_this_profiles` is a
    resource's reading, not a §5 verdict.
  - **`desired.v1` §2.1, §2.17:** "is not this profile's: **not asked**,
    `not_a_target`", and `slices.json` gives `report.found`
    `not_a_target`.
- **So the rule and the fixtures disagree.** A freshness, telemetry or
  desired tool that renders its profile's fixtures breaks §1, and one that
  keeps §1 fails its fixtures. The changelog's "§1's not this profile's
  names a token the profiles published before this text" holds of three
  profiles out of the six that name one. `profiles/README.md`'s template
  lists not this profile's beside the unestablished pair, and settles
  neither reading.
- **Proposal.** One of these:
  - §1 admits both spellings a profile may choose: a kind of its own, or
    NotAsked with a reason naming the premise (`kind`, `deleted`,
    `not_this_profiles`, `not_a_target`). It then says how a tool keeps
    the second apart from a question nobody put;
  - the three profiles move their answers to the token, which changes
    fixtures (freshness's `kind` and `deleted` cases, telemetry's
    conformance, desired's §2.17 row);
  - §1 binds only the profiles whose §5 gives the token.
- **Changes:** the wording, or three profiles' fixtures. No verdict either
  implementation gives today changes. zk2py follows each profile's
  fixtures, and `readings` hold the three spellings (F-291's four cases).

### F-292 · gap · observer §8.2 and grammar.md §1 step 5: which medium states a scope's exclusions

> §8.2: "A tool that offers a wildcard scope either names the verbatim
> kinds it watches beside it, or states that they are excluded."
> grammar.md §1 step 5, expected: "reports `@stream`, `@state`, `@op`,
> `@adv` and `@zk` excluded from its scope, beside what it watched".

- **No medium named.** §1 names three media (a table cell, a report field
  and a note), and "a tool keeps its claims straight in all three".
  Neither §8.2 nor the step names one.
- **Measured** (`observer_scenarios`' grammar §1, both owners):
  - In table output, `zenctl echo zk2/g/**` states the exclusion on
    stderr: "echoing zk2/g/** — @stream, @state, @op, @zk, @adv excluded:
    no selector names them, and `*`/`**` never match one".
  - Under `--format ndjson` it shows the same three samples and says
    nothing, in its rows or on stderr. That holds whether stderr is a pipe
    or a terminal (run under `script`). A script that reads its rows
    cannot tell a scope that excludes the explicit kinds from one that
    names them.
  - `zenctl timing`'s JSON carries `scope` and two notes, and stderr says
    the same.
  - zk2py's echo tool and timing tool state it in the report field, in a
    note and on stderr.
- **Proposal.** §8.2 says the statement reaches every medium the tool
  reports in: a field or a note in a document, an envelope line in a
  stream of rows, and the stream's stderr line. Step 5 checks the report
  field as well as what a person reads.
- **Changes:** the wording, and the reference's ndjson. The two checks are
  XFAIL in `observer_scenarios` (`KNOWN`), by this finding.

### F-293 · minor · observer 0.2 §3.2's transient half and operations.md §8 step 6: the pause is within core §8.2's step 4

> §3.2: "An owner between core §8.2's steps 3 and 4 serves a descriptor
> that lists an interface whose token it has not yet declared."
> operations.md §8 step 6: "serves its descriptor … and holds its instance
> token (core §8.2, step 3), then declares its `tc.v1` token one second
> later (step 4)".

- **Where the instance token is.** Core §8.2's step 3 declares the
  descriptor's queryable and puts it, then the contract queryables. Step
  4 reads "declare the instance token, then the interface tokens", so the
  instance token belongs to step 4.
- **Between steps 3 and 4, a tool sees nothing.** An owner there holds no
  instance token. A tool that finds instances by their tokens, as zk2py's
  and the reference's doctor do, sees no instance and no shape. Measured:
  a descriptor served with no instance token answers its GET, and zk2py's
  tool's read over its address shows no shape.
- **Where the step's shape is.** The shape the step shows (an instance
  token, a descriptor, no interface token) belongs to an owner within
  step 4, between its instance token and its interface tokens, which is
  what the step's owner does.
- **Proposal.** §3.2: "An owner within core §8.2's step 4, between its
  instance token and its interface tokens". Step 6: "holds its instance
  token (core §8.2, step 4), then declares its `tc.v1` token one second
  later (the rest of step 4)".
- **Changes:** wording only.

### observer.md 0.2 in zk2py

- **§3.2's transient half.**
  - `live.presence_faults(…, reads=n, log=…)` reads n times, a grace
    apart, and logs each read's instant and its shapes.
  - `live.shape_faults` pairs each read with the next. A fault is a shape
    that two consecutive reads both saw, and `passing` is every other
    shape seen. A shape seen in two reads, with one between them that did
    not see it, passes.

    after its instance token. With `None` it never declares them, the

### F-295 · gap · observer §1: a NotAsked that spells not this profile's, and what its cell says

> §1, "NotAsked": "nobody put the question. No contract was retrieved, no
> window ran, the flag was not passed. The tool has learned nothing, and
> renders nothing, never the negative answer."
> "The two Unestablished kinds stay apart in every medium. They call for
> different actions: NotAsked is cured by asking, Unobservable by fixing
> the named impediment."
> "Not this profile's": "A profile spells it one of two ways … as a token
> of its own, `not_this_profiles`, kept apart from NotAsked and from
> Unobservable in every medium … as NotAsked with a reason that names the
> failed premise … Either way it is never folded into Unobservable, nor
> into no."

- **The first spelling is kept apart from NotAsked in every medium.** The
  second is NotAsked, and §1 says only that it is never folded into
  Unobservable, nor into no.
- **What §1 says of NotAsked does not hold of the second spelling.** For
  `freshness.v1`'s event, someone did put the question, and the tool
  learned that the subject is not the profile's. Asking again changes
  nothing. `telemetry.v1` §5 widens its own not asked to "nobody put the
  question, or its premise does not hold"; §1's bullet does not.
- **So a tool can drop the reason and meet §1.** A tool that renders
  `freshness.v1`'s event as "not asked" in a table cell, with no reason,
  keeps every rule §1 states. A person reading that cell reads "cured by
  asking", and asks again, to no end. The token's spelling cannot be
  rendered that way.
- **Proposal.** §1 says that a NotAsked of the second spelling carries its
  premise's reason in every medium it reaches, so a cell says not this
  profile's or names the reason. §1's NotAsked bullet then reads "nobody
  put the question, or, for a profile that spells not this profile's so,
  its premise does not hold".
- **zk2py:** `judgement.cell` keeps the reason: "not this profile's (kind),
  spelled not asked".
- **Changes:** the wording, and what a tool's cell shows. No verdict and no
  fixture.

> §2.4: "A contract's author SHOULD set it only on measurement, since it
> can lose samples and gain no latency (spike S9, Appendix B)."
> Appendix B: "spike S9 measured `real_time` + express losing 0.6–4 % of
> samples at 1–5 kHz on loopback, with no latency gain."

> §12, Bundles: "A constrained owner can send one, so the limit is on
> receiving (Appendix B)."
> Appendix B, "One binding's facts": "A zenoh-pico 1.10.1 owner sent
> 100 KB replies, so a constrained device's limit on bundles is on
> receiving (§12)."

- **§2.4.** The reason names `express` alone. Spike S9 measured it beside
  `real_time`, at 1–5 kHz, on loopback.
- **§12.** The reason turns one binding's measurement (zenoh-pico 1.10.1,
  100 KB replies) into a claim about every constrained owner and any
  bundle ("one"). Appendix B files it under "One binding's facts", whose
  heading says a rule's wording allows for it, and the rule's wording
  now states it of every binding.
- **Neither moves a rule.** The SHOULD still asks for a measurement, and a
  gateway holder still serves the bundles. The changelog says each rule
  keeps its reason in words. These two keep a reason wider than its
  ground.
- **Proposal.** §2.4: "since with `real_time` it lost samples and gained no
  latency (spike S9, Appendix B)". §12: "A zenoh-pico owner sent 100 KB
  replies, so the limit is on receiving (Appendix B)".
- **Changes:** wording only.

### Hard to read: F-297 to F-314

Each entry below is a sentence zk2py had to read twice to be sure what it
requires. It quotes the sentence whole, says what made it hard and what
zk2py took it to mean, and proposes a rewrite. Each rewrite keeps the
same keyword, condition, scope and evidence, so its fix is editorial, as
#935's pass was. F-298 is the exception: every rewrite zk2py found has to
choose between two readings, so it is **ambiguous**. None changes a verdict
either implementation gives, and each reading below is the one zk2py
implements.

### F-297 · hard to read · observer §3.3, the MUST at the interests timeout

> "A reader MUST read a read whose time reached its session's interests
> timeout as possibly incomplete, as it reads one that received an error
> reply, and a round trip (below) that ended there as not standing: it was
> asked, so it was made, and what it establishes is nothing."

- **Hard:** one MUST over two objects, each with its own condition and its
  own "as" complement ("read a read … as", "a round trip … as"). "(below)"
  points at §3.7, where the round trip is defined. The reason's "it" could
  be either object.
- **Took:** two duties. A read whose time reached the interests timeout is
  possibly incomplete, like a read with an error reply. A round trip that
  ended at that timeout does not stand. The reason is the round trip's.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A reader MUST read as possibly incomplete a read whose time reached
    its session's interests timeout, as it reads a read that received an
    error reply.
  - A reader MUST read as not standing a round trip (§3.7) that ended at
    that timeout. The round trip was asked, so it was made, but it
    establishes nothing.

  `[Sc: presence.md §10]`

### F-298 · ambiguous · observer §3.3, "meets this by it"

> "A reader whose reads may wait longer SHOULD run its session with an
> interests timeout above the longest it waits for one: its long reads can
> then be complete (core Appendix B). A reader that asks each GET with its
> own timeout at or above the interests timeout (below) bounds that wait
> apart, and meets this by it."

- **Hard:** "that wait", "this" and "it" each point back into the sentence
  before. "(below)" points four subsections on, to §3.7's MAY. And the
  second sentence does not say under what condition its reader meets the
  SHOULD. 0.3 carried an example, "(0.49, F-250: zk2py's follower runs
  120 s and asks its GETs with 121 s)", which 0.4 removed with its tag.
- **Two readings:**
  - **A.** A reader that asks each GET with a timeout at or above the
    interests timeout, and bounds its own wait apart, meets the SHOULD,
    whatever that bound is.
  - **B.** It meets the SHOULD when the bound it sets apart, now the
    longest it waits, is below its session's interests timeout. Under A, a
    reader with a 10 s interests timeout, 11 s GETs and a 30 s wait meets
    the SHOULD, though every read that runs past 10 s ends there and is
    possibly incomplete (the MUST above). That defeats the SHOULD's stated
    reason, "its long reads can then be complete".
- **zk2py reads B**: its follower's waits are its callers' timeouts, below
  the 120 s it runs its sessions with.
- **Every rewrite chooses.** B's: "A reader that asks each GET with its own
  timeout at or above the interests timeout (§3.7) bounds its wait apart
  from the GET. It meets this SHOULD when that bound is below the
  interests timeout." A's: "… meets this SHOULD whatever that bound is."
- **Changes:** the wording. Under A, the SHOULD would ask nothing of such a
  reader. No verdict either implementation gives moves.

### F-299 · hard to read · observer §3.3, a session whose interests timeout cannot be read

> "A reader that cannot read its session's interests timeout SHOULD open
> the session itself with a value it sets, and so knows; a session it is
> handed and cannot read, it takes at zenoh's default, 10 s. That holds
> only of a session whose configuration states none: a lower value ends a
> read sooner, with nothing in the read to show it, so such a reader says
> that its reads' completeness rests on the default."

- **Hard:** "itself" could be the reader or the session. "and so knows"
  has no object. The second clause puts its object first ("a session it
  is handed and cannot read, it takes at"). "That" and "none" each need
  their antecedent found: taking the session at 10 s, and an interests
  timeout. "such a reader" is two clauses back.
- **Took:** the SHOULD is to open the session oneself with a known value.
  A reader handed a session it cannot read assumes 10 s. That assumption
  is right only when the configuration states no value, so the reader
  says its completeness rests on it.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A reader that cannot read its session's interests timeout SHOULD open
    that session itself, with a value it sets, so that it knows the value.
  - A reader handed a session whose interests timeout it cannot read takes
    that timeout as zenoh's default, 10 s. The default is right only when
    the session's configuration states no interests timeout. A lower value
    would end a read sooner, and nothing in the read would show it. So
    such a reader says that its reads' completeness rests on the default.

### F-300 · hard to read · observer §3.5, a read through a session cut off

> "A reader SHOULD NOT make it: before a read, and again when it ends, it
> checks that its session holds a transport to another node, and reports a
> read not made, with that reason, as it reports one possibly incomplete.
> What a read not made would have established is unobservable."

- **Hard:** three "it"s with three antecedents: the read through a session
  cut off, a read, and the reader. And the sentence ties both checks to "a
  read not made", while a check that fails when the read ends finds a read
  that was made: "A read cut off while it runs", below, makes that read
  possibly incomplete.
- **Took:** the check before the read decides whether to make it. The
  check when it ends decides whether the read was cut off while it ran.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A reader SHOULD NOT make such a read. Before each read, and again when
    it ends, the reader checks that its session holds a transport to
    another node.
  - A read the first check stops is not made. The reader reports it so,
    with that reason, as it reports a read possibly incomplete. What it
    would have established is unobservable.
  - A read the second check finds with no link was cut off while it ran
    (below).

### F-301 · hard to read · observer §3.5, "A profile's premise"

> "**A profile's premise.** Where a profile names a presence read possibly
> incomplete or refused, a read not made is read as that premise reads it:
> unobservable. The profile's reason stands, and a tool reports the read's
> own reason beside it (not made: cut off, or beside a liveliness
> subscriber). The kinds stay apart in the tool's report; the profile's
> answer does not change."

- **Hard:** "names" means "names as a premise of one of its answers",
  which the label alone says. "that premise reads it" makes the premise
  the reader. "The kinds" has no antecedent: zk2py took it to be a read
  not made and a read possibly incomplete or refused.
- **Took:** where a profile answers unobservable because a presence read
  was possibly incomplete or refused, a read not made gives the same
  answer, with the profile's reason. The tool reports the read's own
  reason beside it, and keeps a read not made apart from the others in
  its report.
- **Rewrite:**
  - **A profile's premise.** Some profiles answer unobservable where a
    presence read was possibly incomplete or refused. A read not made gives
    the same answer: unobservable, with the profile's reason.
  - Beside the profile's reason, a tool reports the read's own: not made,
    because its session was cut off or because it held a liveliness
    subscriber.
  - The tool's report keeps a read not made apart from one possibly
    incomplete and one refused. The profile's answer does not change.

### F-302 · hard to read · observer §3.6, reading again after a withdrawal

> "A reader that follows presence live SHOULD read again soon after a
> withdrawal that leaves something with nothing held — an address its
> instance tokens, an interface its tokens, a member its epochs — one read
> for a burst of them, and report what that read establishes: absent when
> it is complete and shows none, present when it shows one."

- **Hard:** the list between the dashes leaves out its verb ("an address
  [with none of] its instance tokens"). The sentence carries two duties
  (read again, report) and a permission (one read for a burst). "none"
  and "one" each need their noun found.
- **Took:** after a withdrawal leaves an address with no instance token,
  an interface with no token or a member with no epoch, the reader SHOULD
  read again soon. One read serves a burst of such withdrawals. It reports
  absent when that read is complete and shows no token held, and present
  when it shows one.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A reader that follows presence live SHOULD read again soon after a
    withdrawal that leaves one of these with nothing held:
    - an address, with none of its instance tokens;
    - an interface, with none of its tokens;
    - a member, with none of its epochs.
  - One read serves a burst of such withdrawals. The reader SHOULD report
    what that read establishes: absent when the read is complete and shows
    no token held, present when it shows one.

### F-303 · hard to read · observer §3.7, a wait that ends before the round trip

> "One whose wait ends first reads possibly incomplete (below), as before,
> and before its next read takes up the round trip in flight (below),
> asking another only once that one has ended without standing."

- **Hard:** "One" is a reader, three sentences back. "ends first" means
  "before the round trip's reply". "reads possibly incomplete" has no
  object. "as before" has no antecedent zk2py could find. Two "(below)"s
  point forward, one to a term ("takes up") defined there.
- **Took:** a reader whose wait for the round trip after a move ends
  before the round trip's reply reads what it reads meanwhile as possibly
  incomplete ("A read made while no round trip stands"). Before its next
  read it takes up the round trip still in flight ("One round trip, and
  one read, at a time"). It asks another round trip only once that one
  has ended without standing.
- **Rewrite:** "A reader whose wait ends before the round trip's reply:
  - reads what it reads meanwhile as possibly incomplete, as for any read
    made while no round trip stands (below);
  - before its next read, takes up the round trip still in flight (below,
    "In flight is at the reader");
  - asks another round trip only once that one has ended without
    standing."

### F-304 · hard to read · observer §3.7, where a move begins

> "No withdrawal reaches a session with no link but a close's own telling,
> so a reader that holds back what a move makes it hear SHOULD begin the
> move at its transport event or at a withdrawal its watch hears while the
> watch session holds no link, whichever comes first; one that begins it
> at the event alone applies the close's withdrawals as heard."

- **Hard:** "but" means "except", which a reader finds only at
  "telling". "its transport event" means the watch session's. The clause
  after the semicolon could be a second rule or a consequence of not
  following the first.
- **Took:** only a close's own telling reaches a session with no link, so
  such a withdrawal marks the close. The SHOULD is to begin the move at the
  first of the two instants. The last clause is a consequence: a reader
  that waits for the event applies the close's withdrawals as ordinary
  withdrawals heard.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A session with no link hears no withdrawal except those its own close
    tells.
  - So a reader that holds back what a move makes it hear SHOULD begin the
    move at the first of:
    - its watch session's transport event;
    - a withdrawal its watch hears while the watch session holds no link.
  - A reader that begins the move at the transport event alone applies the
    close's withdrawals as heard.

  `[Sc: profiles/arbitration/scenarios.md §7]`

### F-305 · hard to read · observer §3.7, "In flight is at the reader"

> "A GET its own timeout ends is over for the reader, which zenoh hands an
> error reply and the final reply and nothing after them, and cannot be
> taken up."

- **Hard:** a relative clause with no "that" ("A GET its own timeout
  ends"), then "which" for the reader, then "and cannot be taken up",
  whose subject is the GET again, after the clause about the reader.
- **Took:** such a GET is over. zenoh hands the reader an error reply and
  the final reply, and nothing more. No later read can take it up.
- **Rewrite:** "A GET that its own timeout ends is over for the reader:
  zenoh hands the reader an error reply, then the final reply, and nothing
  after them. Such a GET cannot be taken up."

### F-306 · hard to read · observer §3.7, the namespace's withdrawal

> "In zenoh 1.10.1 a namespaced session does not strip its namespace from
> that key, and its subscriber without history never hears the withdrawal
> (core Appendix B)."

- **Hard:** "that key" and "the withdrawal" point into the previous
  bullet, past its `[Sc:]` and a new bold label: "the router tells its
  withdrawal by its key", for "a token declared before the subscribers
  and withdrawn after the round trip".
- **Took:** a router tells such a withdrawal by the token's wire key. A
  namespaced session does not strip its namespace from that key, so its
  subscriber without history never hears that withdrawal.
- **Rewrite:** "A router tells the withdrawal of a token declared before
  the subscribers by the token's key (above). In zenoh 1.10.1 a namespaced
  session does not strip its namespace from that key. So its subscriber
  without history never hears the withdrawal (core Appendix B)."

### F-307 · hard to read · observer §4.3, the records under `deny`

> "A router under a generated block refuses such a GET from a tool's
> credentials, so a tool its user asks reads nothing of them through it,
> and says the admin space did not answer, never that nothing is
> declared."

- **Hard:** "a tool its user asks" means "a tool whose user asks for that
  read". "them" is the declaration records, two sentences back, and "it"
  is the router.
- **Took:** even asked by its user, a tool reads none of these records
  through such a router, and reports the silence as the admin space not
  answering.
- **Rewrite:** "A router under a generated block refuses such a GET from a
  tool's credentials. So a tool whose user asks for that read reads none
  of these records through that router. It says that the admin space did
  not answer, never that nothing is declared."

### F-308 · hard to read · observer §6.1, the runtime does not fence

> "A tool diagnoses it, and the runtime does not fence, but for an
> interface whose contract uses `redundancy.v1`: its holders step down as
> that profile's §2.9 says, which is no fence either, since writes in
> flight still land (core §6)."

- **Hard:** "but for" reads as an exception to "does not fence", so the
  runtime would fence there. The clause after the colon then says that
  what it does is no fence either.
- **Took:** the runtime fences no interface. Under `redundancy.v1` the
  holders step down, and stepping down is no fence.
- **Rewrite:** "A tool diagnoses it. The runtime does not fence. For an
  interface whose contract uses `redundancy.v1`, its holders step down as
  that profile's §2.9 says. That is no fence either, since writes in flight
  still land (core §6)."

### F-309 · hard to read · observer §7.2, "Told so"

> "**Told so,** the tool holds a silence from an owner whose tokens it
> reads as the finding."

- **Hard:** it reads first as "the tokens it reads as the finding". "as
  the finding" belongs to "holds", six words back.
- **Took:** the tool holds the silence as the finding, where it reads the
  owner's tokens.
- **Rewrite:** "**Told so,** the tool holds as the finding a silence from
  an owner whose tokens it reads."

### F-310 · hard to read · observer §8.2, a scope's exclusions in every medium

> "A tool that offers a wildcard scope either names the verbatim kinds it
> watches beside it, or states that they are excluded, in every medium it
> writes: a field of its report, or, for a stream of rows that has no
> place for one (NDJSON), its standard error."

- **Hard:** "in every medium it writes" could bind both alternatives or
  the second alone. "beside it" means beside the scope. "one" means a
  field. The list after the colon names two media, where §1 names three (a
  table cell, a report field and a note). A table is not named, though it
  is a stream of rows with no place for a field too.
- **Took:** both alternatives, in every medium. `grammar.md` §1 step 5's
  Expected settles this: what the tool watched and what it excluded, "in
  every medium it writes". A table rendering states it on standard error,
  as the reference's `zenctl echo` does.
- **Rewrite:** "A tool that offers a wildcard scope does one of these, in
  every medium it writes:
  - it names, beside the scope, the verbatim kinds it watches;
  - it states that they are excluded.

  A report carries the statement in a field. A stream of rows with no
  place for a field (NDJSON) carries it on the tool's standard error.
  `[Sc: grammar.md §1]`"

### F-311 · hard to read · observer §5.2, the watch after a window

> "A tool watches the owner's instance tokens for one lease after the
> window's end, zenoh's default being 10 s, and its reply timeout more for
> the withdrawal's transit."

- **Hard:** the aside "zenoh's default being 10 s" splits the duration in
  two. "and its reply timeout more" leaves out "for": the reader has to
  rebuild "for one lease … and for its reply timeout more".
- **Took:** the watch lasts one lease (10 s by default) plus the tool's
  reply timeout, for the withdrawal's transit.
- **Rewrite:** "After the window's end, a tool watches the owner's instance
  tokens for one lease plus its reply timeout. The lease is 10 s by
  default, and the reply timeout allows for the withdrawal's transit."

### F-312 · hard to read · core §8.5, a far router in a south region (0.60's wording)

> "Declarations then cross on interest, and the deny keeps the denied
> families off the link, where router to router they would cross (spike
> S3, Appendix B)."

- **Hard:** "where" reads as a place on the link, and means "whereas". 0.60
  wrote the clause in place of "200 denied tokens cost 506 B, against
  11.3 KB router to router".
- **Took:** in a south region the deny keeps the denied declarations off
  the link. On a router-to-router link they would cross despite it.
- **Rewrite:** "Declarations then cross on interest, and the deny keeps the
  denied families off the link. Router to router, they would cross it
  (spike S3, Appendix B)."

### F-313 · hard to read · core §11.1, a wider admin read

> "A wider admin read, `@/*/router` and `@/*/router/**`, would admit a GET
> of every record of a router's (a peer's and a client's it never
> reaches), and would refuse `@/*/*`, which neither key includes."

- **Hard:** "of a router's" ends in a possessive with no noun. The
  parenthesis interrupts with its own "it", which is the read. "which" is
  `@/*/*`, after a comma that could also attach it to the GET.
- **Took:** such a read admits a GET of every record of a router, reaches
  no peer's or client's records, and refuses a GET of `@/*/*`, which
  neither of its keys includes.
- **Rewrite:**
  - A wider admin read, `@/*/router` and `@/*/router/**`, would admit a
    GET of every one of a router's records. It never reaches a peer's
    records, nor a client's.
  - It would refuse a GET of `@/*/*`, which neither of its keys includes.

### F-314 · hard to read · core §4.3 and §12, 0.60's pointers "(X: Appendix B)"

> §4.3: "A larger step keeps the rule, which needs only that each stamp
> exceed the last (a binding's smallest step: Appendix B)."
> §12: "| Descriptor (§3.3) | MUST fit one fragment (its size: Appendix B)
> `[Sc: constrained.md §5]` |"

- **Hard:** the pointer reads as a definition ("its size: Appendix B").
  §12's "its size" names no binding, and Appendix B gives the size for one
  binding alone ("4 KB with zenoh-pico's default `Z_FRAG_MAX_SIZE`").
  §4.3's names no binding either, where Appendix B gives zenoh-python's.
- **Took:** Appendix B, "One binding's facts", gives zenoh-python's
  smallest step (1 ns) and zenoh-pico's default fragment (4 KB). The rules
  are binding-neutral.
- **Rewrite:** §4.3: "A larger step keeps the rule, which needs only that
  each stamp exceed the last (Appendix B gives zenoh-python's smallest
  step)." §12: "MUST fit one fragment (Appendix B gives its size under
  zenoh-pico's default)".

### observer.md 0.3 in zk2py

- **§1's two spellings** (`zk2py.judgement`, new).
  - `judgement.read(profile, answer, reasons)` reads a profile's answer, as
    its fixtures write it, into §1's shape: Established, NotAsked,
    Unobservable, or not this profile's. Not this profile's is the token
    `not_this_profiles` from any profile, or a `not_asked` whose reason is
    one §1 names for that profile (`SPELLINGS`: `kind` and `deleted` for
    `freshness.v1`, `not_this_profiles` for `telemetry.v1`,
    `not_a_target` for `desired.v1`). Every other `not_asked` is NotAsked,
    and a premise reason binds only the profile that names it.
  - The three media: `cell` (what a person scans), `field` (the profile's
    token and reasons kept, beside `shape`) and `note`. Not this profile's
    says so in each, never Unobservable and never a negative pole. A
    NotAsked of the second spelling keeps its reason in the cell (F-295).
  - `judgement.answers(doc)` walks a fixture file's answers. The readings
    read all six fixtures §1 cites.
- **§8.2's medium** (`zk2py.echo_tool --format ndjson`). Each sample is one
  JSON line as it arrives, the row `samples` holds and nothing else. The
  scope (what it watched, the verbatim kinds it excluded) goes to standard
  error in every format (`scope_line`), before the first row. The JSON
  document keeps it in its `scope` field, as before. `--count` now stops
  the rows at the count.
- **`readings`:** 640, up from 609. 31 cases: the six fixtures' answers by
  shape and spelling (11, 9 and 5 tokens; 6, 1 and 8 premise reasons), the
  other `not_asked` reasons of each, nine single readings, the three media,
  and the echo tool's NDJSON row and stderr line.
- **`just py-conformance`: 3597 of 3597.**
- **`observer_scenarios`** checks zk2py's echo tool in NDJSON beside its
  JSON document, and `zenctl echo --format ndjson`'s stdout for rows alone.
  `KNOWN` is empty.
- **After review-bot on PR #955** (nothing blocking; its should-fixes):
  - In NDJSON, zenoh's callback only queues each row (`echo_tool.Rows`),
    and the main thread writes it, so a reader slow to take standard
    output never stalls the session's delivery.
  - A write that fails (a closed pipe, any `OSError` on stdout) is the
    stream cut: the tool says "echo: the stream was cut: …" on stderr and
    exits 2, never 0 on a truncated stream. `observer_scenarios` checks it
    with each owner, the tool's stdout closed by its reader.
  - `judgement.SPELLINGS` holds only the NotAsked-spelled profiles and
    their premise reasons, `TOKEN_SPELLED` the three others, and a
    reading holds the two to the six fixtures §1 cites. The pinned
    fixture counts are a deliberate tripwire, which a comment says.
  - `readings` 645 (five more: the hand-off, the cut stream and the two
    lists). `just py-conformance`: 3602 of 3602. `observer_scenarios`: 48
    of 48.

## At observer.md 0.5 and core 0.61: round 84's answers, and every long sentence split (#935)

Round 85 read `spec/observer.md` text 0.5 whole and cold, and core 0.61's
changed sections, on main c9bde0af (PR #956). It checked F-295 to F-314,
checked the claim that #935's second pass changed no rule but F-295's
wording, implemented F-295 where zk2py's tools showed a bare not asked,
and ran the live runners. It read for **hard to read** throughout. The
reference's parties and tool ran as black boxes (`owner`, `consume` and
`zenctl` in `/srv/dev/targets/zenkey-tier/blackbox/`, built 2026-10-30
04:52), their source never read. It read, as a newcomer would:
- `spec/observer.md` 0.5 whole, and `observer-CHANGELOG.md`'s 0.5 entry;
- `spec/CHANGELOG.md`'s 0.61 entry, and every line 0.61 changed in
  `core.md`, each with the section around it;
- for §1's F-295 rule, the three fixtures it cites; for §3.5, the
  profiles' presence premises (`health.v1`, `alarms.v1`, `desired.v1`,
  `config.v1`, `redundancy.v1`); for §5.2, `scenarios/budget.md` §1 and
  core Appendix B's "What a path drops".

Since round 84, `spec/` changed in five commits: beebb871 (core 0.61),
e7fa32b7 (observer 0.5), 904e6fc2 (`spec/.prose-baseline.json`),
a97700ed and 07c91c81 (§3.3's example: which time it measures). zk2py
diffed `core.md` and `observer.md` against 692de94a, the merge of PR
#955. No fixture, scenario or schema changed, and `examples/zk2/` did
not. zk2py did not run `scripts/check-spec-prose.py`.

Reading A has no sentence left to stand on. **Now unambiguous**, but for one word of the first item, "that timeout", which the second item settles (F-316). |

### No rule changed: the check

**Every RFC 2119 sentence, before and after.** zk2py split both texts
into sentences keyed by section, as in round 84 (a scratch splitter that
reads a table cell as running text, so its core totals are not the
changelog's). It kept each one holding MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD
NOT, MAY, RECOMMENDED, REQUIRED or SHALL.
- **Observer:** 39 before and 43 after, 31 unchanged. Eight changed, and
  four more are second halves of a split. That is the changelog's count
  exactly.
- **Core:** 161 before and 161 after, 158 unchanged and 3 changed. The
  changelog counts 152 and 149: the same three.
- **Each changed sentence, read against its old text:**

| Text | § | Keyword | 0.4 or 0.60 | 0.5 or 0.61 | Moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| observer | §3.3 | MUST (a read at the interests timeout) | "read a read whose time reached … as possibly incomplete, as it reads one that received an error reply" | "read as possibly incomplete a read whose time reached …, as it reads a read that received an error reply" | nothing |
| observer | §3.3 | MUST (a round trip at it), now its own | "and a round trip (below) that ended there as not standing" | "MUST read as not standing a round trip (§3.7) that ended at that timeout" | nothing: "there" was the interests timeout |
| observer | §3.3 | SHOULD (open the session) | "open the session itself with a value it sets, and so knows" | "be the one that opens that session, with an interests timeout it sets, so that it knows the value" | nothing |
| observer | §3.5 | SHOULD NOT (a read through a session cut off) | "make it: before a read, and again when it ends, it checks …, and reports a read not made" | "make such a read"; the first check stops a read not made, the second finds one cut off while it ran | nothing: "A read cut off while it runs" said the second already |
| observer | §3.6 | SHOULD (read again), SHOULD (report), was one | "read again soon after … — one read for a burst of them, and report what that read establishes" | two SHOULDs; "One read serves a burst of such withdrawals" | nothing (below) |
| observer | §3.7 | SHOULD (a session that never held a subscriber), SHOULD (the watch session), was one | "…(one undeclared leaves its session exposed), and hold its liveliness subscribers on another session" | two SHOULDs; "One undeclared still leaves its session exposed." | nothing |
| observer | §3.7 | SHOULD (where a move begins) | "at its transport event or at a withdrawal …, whichever comes first" | "at the first of two instants: its watch session's transport event, or a withdrawal …" | nothing |
| observer | §3.7 | SHOULD NOT (a round trip in flight), SHOULD NOT (a read in flight), was one | "…is in flight, nor ask a read while one it asked of the same scope is" | two SHOULD NOTs | nothing |
| observer | §3.7 | SHOULD NOT (a read through a watch session cut off) | "a read it would follow from it" | "a read that it would follow from that watch session" | nothing |
| core | §2.4 | SHOULD (`express` on measurement) | "since it can lose samples and gain no latency" | "since with `real_time` it lost samples and gained no latency" | the reason narrowed (F-296); the rule kept |
| core | §8.5 | MUST (`declare_queryable` on egress) | one sentence with its reason and the inclusion check | "It learns of queryables only from the declarations the near router sends it. So the far side's principal MUST …, as the owner declares it. A declaration is checked by inclusion …" | nothing |
| core | §12 | MUST (one fragment) | "(its size: Appendix B)" | "(Appendix B gives its size under zenoh-pico's default)" | nothing (F-314) |

**The rest of what changed, not only the keyword sentences.** zk2py read
the word diff of both texts whole: 97 lines of `core.md` and 303 of
`observer.md` in the diff's count. Besides the table and the findings' rewrites, the pass
split the preamble's two sentences, §0's scope (now a list), §1's "not
this profile's" (its examples now "for example"), §3.6's
`arbitration.v1` sentence, §3.7's open and its watch session cut off,
§4.4's owner's stamp ("Those are"), §5.2's "What a deployment provides"
(a list), and in the core §2.7's and §8.1's "At scale", §4.2's "Observing
S1", §5.1's concrete call, §10's list of profiles and five lines of
Appendix B. None moves a condition, an object or a scope. Two needed a
second look:
- **§3.5, "A profile's premise".** 0.4: "Where a profile names a presence
  read possibly incomplete or refused, a read not made is read as that
  premise reads it: unobservable." 0.5: "Some profiles answer unobservable
  where a presence read was possibly incomplete or refused. A read not
  made gives the same answer". The new text would be narrower if a
  profile named such a read with another answer. None does: `health.v1`
  and `alarms.v1` answer unobservable, `presence_incomplete`; `desired.v1`
  answers it `author_presence_incomplete`; `config.v1` and
  `redundancy.v1` read it as unobservable too. No scope moved.
- **§3.6, "one read for a burst of them".** It sat inside the one
  SHOULD, and F-302 read it as a permission. 0.5 states it without a
  keyword: "One read serves a burst of such withdrawals." Read the other
  way, as a SHOULD to coalesce, it asks no more than §3.7's "It SHOULD
  NOT ask a read while one it asked of the same scope is in flight".
  zk2py's follower makes one read per burst either way.

**F-295's wording is the one rule gained**, and the changelog names it.
F-298's three items restore 0.3's meaning, which zk2py implemented all
along. **No rule zk2py implements changed.** Round 82's table of the
rules zk2py implements holds for 0.5 and 0.61 row by row. No section
moved, so every citation in zk2py's modules still leads to its rule.

**The long sentences.** By zk2py's splitter, no sentence of either text's
prose is over 50 words. Its count finds three in observer 0.5 and twelve
in core 0.61: table cells, observer §4.3's key expression (a code span
with a space in it), and two Appendix B lines whose bold label puts them
at 55 and 53 words (50 and 46 without it). The changelogs count prose
alone, so their claim holds.

### F-315 · hard to read · observer §1, NotAsked's bullet beside the second spelling

> "**NotAsked:** nobody put the question. No contract was retrieved, no
> window ran, the flag was not passed. The tool has learned nothing, and
> renders nothing, never the negative answer. A profile can also spell
> not this profile's as NotAsked (below): there the question was put, and
> its premise does not hold."

- **Hard:** a term with two meanings. The bullet says three things of
  NotAsked: nobody put the question, the tool learned nothing, it renders
  nothing. Its last sentence then names a NotAsked of which the first is
  untrue, and leaves the reader to decide whether the other two hold of
  it. The rule below answers: "That NotAsked keeps its reason in every
  medium". So "renders nothing" does not hold of it, and neither does the
  next bullet's "NotAsked is cured by asking".
- **Took:** the bullet's first three sentences are of NotAsked proper. A
  profile's `not_asked` that spells not this profile's was asked, the tool
  learned that the premise fails, and it renders that reason. Asking again
  does not cure it. "Renders nothing" means it renders no answer.
- **Rewrite:**
  - "**NotAsked:** nobody put the question. No contract was retrieved, no
    window ran, the flag was not passed. The tool has learned nothing, and
    renders no answer, never the negative one."
  - "A profile can also spell not this profile's as NotAsked (below).
    There the question was put, and its premise does not hold. What this
    bullet says of NotAsked does not hold of that spelling, and asking
    again does not cure it."
- **Changes:** wording only. No keyword, and no verdict.

### F-316 · hard to read · observer §3.3, "apart from that timeout"

> "A reader that asks each GET with its own timeout at or above the
> interests timeout (§3.7) bounds its own wait for the read apart from
> that timeout."

- **Hard:** a pronoun with two possible antecedents. The sentence names
  two timeouts before "that timeout": the GET's own, and the interests
  timeout, the nearer. The next item, "never the GET's own timeout", and
  the changelog, "bounds its wait apart from the GET's timeout", both mean
  the GET's own.
- **Took:** the GET's own timeout.
- **Rewrite:** "… bounds its own wait for the read apart from the GET's
  own timeout."
- **Changes:** wording only. It is the one word F-298's restored items
  leave to settle.

### F-317 · hard to read · observer §3.7, "without it is one round trip"

> "**The watch session's subscribers SHOULD have no history** when their
> reader seeds by a read on its other session: the round trip's final
> reply follows their history, so with history it waits for the
> population, and without it is one round trip (core Appendix B)."

- **Hard:** a garden path. "Without it" reads first as "without the
  round trip", or as "without the history" with "is one round trip" left
  without a subject. The subject is "it", the round trip, which the clause
  does not name: "and without [history] it is one round trip". Earlier,
  "with history it waits" uses "it" for the round trip as well.
- **Took:** with history, the round trip waits for the population.
  Without history, it is one round trip.
- **Rewrite:** "… when their reader seeds by a read on its other session.
  The round trip's final reply follows their history. So with history the
  round trip waits for the population, and without history it is one
  round trip (core Appendix B)."
- **Changes:** wording only.

### F-318 · hard to read · observer §3.7, the wait for the round trip after a move

> "A reader SHOULD wait for the round trip after a move, and run its
> interests timeout, above that time at its population: about what a
> session's first read of the population costs, every matching token sent
> once."

- **Hard:**
  - One SHOULD over two acts, "wait" and "run", which 0.5 split
    everywhere else in §3.7.
  - "Wait for the round trip … above that time" is split by a second
    verb phrase. The commas make "above that time at its population" a
    complement of both verbs.
  - "That time" points at the bullet before, "the first after each
    reopen of its transport, which waits for the reopening's telling",
    which names a wait, not a time.
- **Took:** the reader SHOULD wait for the round trip after a move longer
  than the reopening's telling takes at its population. It SHOULD run its
  session's interests timeout above that time too. That time is about
  what a session's first read of the population costs.
- **Rewrite:** "A reader SHOULD wait for the round trip after a move
  longer than the reopening's telling takes at its population. It SHOULD
  run its interests timeout above that time too. That time is about what
  a session's first read of the population costs, every matching token
  sent once."
- **Changes:** wording only. The keyword, the condition (a move) and the
  scope (a reader that waits for that round trip) are kept, as two
  SHOULDs.

### F-319 · hard to read · observer §3.7, "The next that needs one"

> "The next that needs one takes up the one in flight, whichever wait
> ended first, its caller's or the reader's own."

- **Hard:**
  - "The next" has no noun: it could be a read, a caller or a need.
  - "One" stands in turn for a round trip or a read, from the two SHOULD
    NOTs before it.
  - "Whichever wait ended first" does not say a wait for what, nor first
    before what.
- **Took:** a round trip or a read of a scope is in flight, and its wait
  has ended. The next time the reader needs one, it takes up the one in
  flight, whether its caller's wait for that one ended or its own.
- **Rewrite:** "When the reader next needs a round trip, or a read of
  that scope, it takes up the one in flight. It does so whichever wait
  for that one ended: its caller's, or its own."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's follower does this (presence §10
  step 10's "taken up" counts).

### F-320 · ambiguous · observer §5.2, "lengthens it": a `wait_before_close` longer than the lease

> "After the window's end, a tool watches the owner's instance tokens for
> one lease plus its reply timeout. The lease is 10 s by default, and the
> reply timeout allows for the withdrawal's transit. A deployment that
> sets a longer lease, or a `wait_before_close` longer than its lease,
> lengthens it."

- **Hard:**
  - "It" is the watch, two sentences back, past "the lease", "the reply
    timeout" and "the withdrawal's transit". F-311's split moved it a
    sentence further from its antecedent.
  - The watch's length, "one lease plus its reply timeout", names no
    `wait_before_close`. So the sentence says what lengthens the watch,
    and not to what.
- **Two readings,** for a `wait_before_close` longer than the lease:
  - **A.** The watch is the longer of the two, plus the reply timeout.
    A push that waits on a full queue closes its transport only after
    `wait_before_close` (core Appendix B, "What a path drops": "the
    owner's own push had waited `wait_before_close` too, and its session
    closed its transport to its router"), so a failure shows within the
    longer of the two.
  - **B.** The watch is the lease plus `wait_before_close`, plus the reply
    timeout: the lengthening added to the lease rather than put in its
    place.
- **Every rewrite chooses.** A's: "A deployment that sets a longer lease
  lengthens the watch. One whose `wait_before_close` is longer than its
  lease watches for that `wait_before_close` in place of the lease, plus
  the reply timeout." B's: "… adds its `wait_before_close` to the lease."
- **Not in zk2py until now.** zk2py's window watched one lease plus the
  reply timeout, whatever `wait_before_close` was. That is too short under
  either reading. It now reads **A** (`budget.watch_after_s`).
- **Where it shows.** Under zenoh's defaults (5 s against a 10 s lease)
  both readings are the lease. `scenarios/budget.md` §1's tool window
  runs a 1 s lease beside the default 5 s `wait_before_close`, which is
  the case the clause names. zk2py's watch after that window is now 6 s,
  not 2 s (B would give 7 s). Its owner stays present, so no verdict
  moves there.
- **Changes:** an implementation, and a test's length. A verdict moves
  only where `wait_before_close` exceeds the lease and the owner fails
  within the longer watch. A watch that is too short reads the owner as
  present throughout, and the window as complete.

### F-321 · hard to read · observer §8.2, "they" and "it" in the scope's exclusions

> "A tool that offers a wildcard scope does one of two things, in every
> medium it writes:
> - it names, beside the scope, the verbatim kinds it watches;
> - or it states that they are excluded.
>
> A report carries it in a field. A stream of rows with no place for a
> field (NDJSON) carries it on the tool's standard error."

- **Hard:** two pronouns, each with the wrong antecedent nearest.
  - "They" has one antecedent, "the verbatim kinds it watches", and a
    tool cannot both watch them and state that they are excluded. It means
    the verbatim kinds of the list above, those the scope never reaches.
  - "Carries it" has two: the names of the first item, or the statement
    of the second. F-310's rewrite said "the statement"; 0.5 kept "it".
- **Took:** a tool names the verbatim kinds it watches, or states that
  the verbatim kinds are excluded. A report carries whichever it does in a
  field, and NDJSON carries it on standard error.
- **Rewrite:**
  - "it names, beside the scope, the verbatim kinds it watches;
  - or it states that the verbatim kinds are excluded.

  A report carries the names or the statement in a field. A stream of
  rows with no place for a field (NDJSON) carries them on the tool's
  standard error."
- **Changes:** wording only. Both of zk2py's tools and `zenctl echo` do
  this (`observer_scenarios`, grammar.md §1 step 5).

### F-322 · hard to read · core 0.61 §4.2, "Observing S1": "It checks the check"

> "A tester therefore runs the owner as a client of a router with
> timestamping enabled, which keeps the stamp a put carries unless it is
> future-dated (§4.1). It checks the check against a control: a put
> without a timestamp, from a session whose HLC is not enabled (§4.1),
> through the same router, arrives with the router's zid."

- **Hard:** a pronoun with several antecedents. 0.61 split one sentence
  here, so "It" now begins a sentence. The nouns before it are "the
  owner", "a router" and "it is future-dated" (the stamp). The tester,
  two clauses back, is meant.
- **Took:** the tester checks the check against the control.
- **Rewrite:** "The tester checks the check against a control: …".
- **Changes:** wording only. It describes a tester's method, with no
  keyword. zk2py runs it (`state_scenarios`, state.md §1).

### F-323 · hard to read · core §8.5, "For a state GET that is the owner's state queryables"

> "For a state GET that is the owner's state queryables over `state/**`
> and `@state/**` (S2); for a call, the operation's queryable on its
> concrete key or over its template (O1), `@op/set/*` for a call of
> `set/duty`; for an archive, its `@state` forms (§4.4)."

- **Hard:**
  - A garden path. "A state GET that is the owner's state queryables"
    reads as a relative clause, a GET that is queryables. The "that" is a
    demonstrative for the MUST's "every queryable its side may query", two
    sentences back.
  - The verb is left out after the first item.
- **Took:** the queryables the grant covers are, for a state GET, the
  owner's state queryables over `state/**` and `@state/**`; for a call,
  the operation's queryable; for an archive, its `@state` forms.
- **Rewrite:** "The queryables the grant covers are:
  - for a state GET, the owner's state queryables over `state/**` and
    `@state/**` (S2);
  - for a call, the operation's queryable on its concrete key or over its
    template (O1): `@op/set/*` for a call of `set/duty`;
  - for an archive, its `@state` forms (§4.4)."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's generator emits no face declarations
  (README, "What it does not cover").

- **F-295 in zk2py's tools.** `judgement.cell` already kept the reason

  timeout. A caller's own `lease_s` in `Window.reading` is read the same

- **`readings`: 653, up from 645.** Eight cases:

  - their 15 NotAsked answers that spell not this profile's (6, 1 and 8);

### After review-bot on PR #957

Nothing was blocking. The bot's should-fix and nits:
- **The member field's callers** (`freshness.py`). `read_service`'s
  member value changed from a token string to `{"verdict", "reason"}`.
  Its callers are `freshness_scenarios` §6 and `live_interop`'s
  freshness run, and no report writer or other tool calls it. Both
  printed the member map without reading it. Each now reads it through
  `freshness.service_members`, which checks every field through
  `member_verdicts`, and adds a check of its own. Each resource's one
  member is judged as its resource is, and the interop run's `level`
  has none.
  - The boundary is typed both ways. `member_fields` refuses a member
    that is not a `Verdict`. `member_verdicts` refuses anything but
    exactly `verdict` and `reason`, both strings, the verdict one of §5's
    tokens: round 84's bare token, a field without its reason, one with
