### F-324 · gap · observer §5.2, the watch's `wait_before_close` item: the reason claims more than its scenario shows

> "- **`wait_before_close`** is the deployment's too, 5 s by default. A
>   push that cannot queue within it closes its transport (core Appendix
>   B, "What a path drops"). So a router that waits it before closing a
>   transport tells the withdrawal that late, when it is longer than the
>   lease."

- **The gap: no scenario shows the half of the rule that 0.6 settled.**
  - The rule cites `[Sc: budget.md §2]`. That section runs a 1 s lease
    beside zenoh's default 5 s `wait_before_close`, so a
    `wait_before_close` longer than the lease, the very case the item
    names.
  - It measures the withdrawal one lease after a stall began, 986 to
    1,037 ms, never at `wait_before_close`. Its links close or go silent,
    and neither makes a push wait on a full queue.
  - The mechanism is measured elsewhere: `budget.md` §1 step 3's router
    gives up on a stalled consumer after `wait_before_close` (5 s), and
    core Appendix B's "the owner's own push had waited
    `wait_before_close` too, and its session closed its transport". Both
    ran beside zenoh's default 10 s lease, so before it.
  - So no measurement shows a withdrawal told later than one lease. The
    scenario the rule cites shows a router whose `wait_before_close` is
    above its lease telling it one lease late.
- **Hard to read too.** "Waits it" takes a duration as its object.
  "That late" is a time the sentence does not name: `wait_before_close`
  after the failure. "It" in "when it is longer" is `wait_before_close`,
  two clauses back past "a router" and "a transport". The condition comes
  last.
- **Took:** a push that cannot queue within `wait_before_close` closes
  the transport it pushes on. A path that stays up while its queue is
  full keeps its lease, so the withdrawal it causes can reach the reader
  up to `wait_before_close` after the failure. A silent link's comes one
  lease after it. The watch covers the later of the two.
- **Rewrite:**
  - "**`wait_before_close`** is the deployment's too, 5 s by default. A
    push that cannot queue within it closes the transport it pushes on
    (core Appendix B, "What a path drops"). A path that stays up while its
    queue is full keeps its lease. So its withdrawal can reach the reader
    up to `wait_before_close` after the failure, later than a silent
    link's when `wait_before_close` is longer than the lease."
  - And evidence for that half: a step of `budget.md` §2 that fills a
    queue on a path that stays up (a router whose receive is slowed, its
    keep-alives still crossing), and measures when the owner's token is
    withdrawn. Or the item says that this half rests on Appendix B's
    mechanism alone, with no measurement.
- **Changes:** a test (a scenario step) and wording. The rule's length
  is unchanged, and zk2py has it. A longer watch can only leave a window
  incomplete that a shorter one would call complete, so it errs toward
  unobservable.

### F-325 · hard to read · observer §1, "What this bullet says of NotAsked"

> "- **NotAsked:** nobody put the question. No contract was retrieved, no
>   window ran, the flag was not passed. The tool has learned nothing, and
>   renders no answer, never the negative one.
>   - A profile can also spell not this profile's as NotAsked (below).
>     There the question was put, and its premise does not hold. What this
>     bullet says of NotAsked does not hold of that spelling, and asking
>     again does not cure it."

- **Hard:** a term with two referents. "This bullet" is either the item
  that holds the sentence, or NotAsked's bullet above it. Read as the
  item, the sentence says that "the question was put" does not hold of
  the spelling it has just described. The words are zk2py's own, from
  F-315's rewrite, where the second spelling was a bullet of its own and
  "this bullet" named itself, which was no better. 0.6 made it an item
  inside NotAsked's bullet, which leaves the word two referents.
- **Took:** NotAsked's bullet: nobody put the question, the tool learned
  nothing, it renders no answer.
- **Rewrite:** "What NotAsked's bullet says above (nobody put the
  question, the tool has learned nothing, and it renders no answer) does
  not hold of that spelling, and asking again does not cure it."
- **Changes:** wording only.

> "The text keeps its version, as it did for core 0.38's F-187. The rule
> is observer §5.2's, which this text restated." (`alarms/CHANGELOG.md`,
> "0.8, read against observer.md 0.6")

- **The issue:**

### F-327 · hard to read · `health.v1` scenarios, Conventions, "T's clock"

> "A tool in a deployment takes that word only as its operator's option
> (`freshness.v1` §2.6). Without it, a tool measures its clock from puts
> it hears during its reading, and the status is re-put every 30 s, so
> the reading lasts 30 s, or its subscription is declared before the
> owners start."

- **Hard:** a requirement stated as a fact, and an "or" that joins a
  duration to a precondition. "So the reading lasts 30 s" reads as what
  every such reading does.
- **Took:** a tool without the deployment's word needs a put of the
  owner's clock to measure from. The status is re-put every 30 s. So its
  reading must last 30 s, unless its subscription was declared before
  the owners started, when it hears their first puts.
- **Rewrite:** "Without it, a tool measures its clock from puts it hears
  during its reading. The status is re-put every 30 s. So such a tool's
  reading lasts 30 s, unless its subscription is declared before the
  owners start."
- **Changes:** wording only. It is a runner's convention, which
  zk2py's §5 to §7 do not need: T takes the word.

### F-328 · hard to read · `hostid.v1` §2.12, "Undecided", its third item

> "- **Undecided.** The address is unobservable, never clean, when the
>   instances that could be counted do not establish the finding, and an
>   instance's descriptor:
>   - could not be read;
>   - or states no `meta.zid`;
>   - or lists `hostid.v1` while whether its system is minted is
>     unobservable, by §5's first question: a contract it implements
>     lists `hostid.v1` in `uses`, or could not be read;
>   - or lists only governed interfaces while `redundancy.v1`'s question
>     is unobservable for one of them."

- **Hard:** a subject left out. Every item continues "an instance's
  descriptor", and the first is "could not be read". The third ends "or
  could not be read", which reads first as the descriptor again. Its
  subject is "a contract it implements", from §5's first question ("a
  contract it implements could not be read (core §8.4)"). 0.8's list put
  the two "could not be read" side by side, where 0.7's parenthesis kept
  them apart.
- **Took:** §5's first question is unobservable when a contract the
  instance implements lists `hostid.v1` in `uses`, or when a contract it
  implements could not be read.
- **Rewrite:** "- or lists `hostid.v1` while §5's first question is
  unobservable for it: a contract it implements lists `hostid.v1` in
  `uses`, or a contract it implements could not be read;"
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `live.hostid_collision` reads it so
  (scenarios §6 step 5).

### F-329 · hard to read · `config.v1` §2.3, "Two keys, one revision"

> "So `instance` and `revision` name the running values, never a pair: a
> reader that reads both pairs them only when the status is the view's
> projection (§2.19), and otherwise takes each by itself, judged by its
> own freshness."

- **Hard:**
  - "A pair" and "pairs them" name different things.
  - "Both" and "them" have two antecedents: `instance` and `revision`,
    the sentence's subject, or the view and the status, the paragraph's.
  - "The status is the view's projection" is §2.19's MUST of every
    status, so the condition reads as always true. It means the status
    the reader read is the projection of the view it read.
- **Took:** an `instance` and a `revision` do not name one version of the
  two documents, since an arm or a confirm re-puts both at the same
  revision. A reader that read the view and the status takes them as one
  reading only when the status it read is the projection of the view it
  read. Otherwise it judges each by its own freshness.
- **Rewrite:** "So `instance` and `revision` name the running values,
  never one version of the two documents. A reader that reads the view
  and the status takes them together only when the status it read is the
  projection of the view it read (§2.19). Otherwise it takes each by
  itself, judged by its own freshness."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's §5 reader (`config.read`) takes each
  by itself.

### F-330 · hard to read · `config.v1` §2.13, persist's first refusal

> "1. no persisted layer: `unavailable`, cause `config`. An owner with
>    none does not expose `persist`, and the core refuses the call so
>    before any handler runs, its request's type included (below). A layer
>    it cannot write to now is refused the same way, first of the
>    handler's refusals: before the request's type too, so that the
>    refusal does not depend on whether the layer was ever there;"

- **Hard:**
  - "So" stands for the refusal the item opens with.
  - "Its request's type included" is an absolute phrase. It means
    "before even the check of its request's type", and reads first as
    the request's type included in the refusal.
  - "(below)" points at the bullet "No persisted layer", past the rest of
    the list and three more bullets.
- **Took:** an owner with no persisted layer lists `persist` unavailable.
  So the core answers `unavailable`, cause `config`, before any handler
  runs, and so before the request's type is checked. An owner whose layer
  cannot be written now refuses the same way, in its handler, first of its
  refusals and before it checks the request's type.
- **Rewrite:** "1. no persisted layer: `unavailable`, cause `config`:
   - An owner with none does not expose `persist`. The core refuses the
     call so before any handler runs, and so before it checks the
     request's type ("No persisted layer", below).
   - A layer it cannot write to now is refused the same way by the
     handler, before its other refusals and before the request's type.
     The refusal then does not depend on whether the layer was ever
     there;"
- **Changes:** wording only. `validation.json` pins the order, and zk2py
  meets it.

### F-331 · hard to read · `config.v1` §2.18, "A delete": "a refused document's aside"

> "Each parameter named by a document it acted on in this instance, a
> refused document's aside, goes back to its startup value (§2.12)."

- **Hard:** an absolute phrase with its noun left out. Aside what of a
  refused document: the document, or its parameters? 0.6's split made
  the phrase the middle of a sentence of its own. It could mean that a
  refused document is not among those acted on, so that a parameter a
  converged document named reverts whatever a later refused one named.
  Or it could mean that a refused document's parameters stay out even
  where a converged document named them. The second would leave a
  converged value standing after the delete, against `desired.v1` §2.16's
  baseline, "what a restart would start it from". So the first, and the
  sentence is hard to read, not ambiguous.
- **Took:** a document the owner refused counts for nothing: it applied
  none of it.
- **Rewrite:** "Each parameter named by a document it acted on in this
  instance goes back to its startup value (§2.12). A document it refused
  counts for none: it applied nothing of it (above)."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's config owner converges a document
  bound to it directly (scenarios §12). It is never fed through
  `desired.v1`, so it reverts nothing, and no test of zk2py's reads this.

### F-332 · hard to read · `link.v1` §2.4, "Not in a policy of its own"

> "That is the mechanism for which core §11.2 compiles "every principal"
> into each principal's own policy. In the far principal's policy it
> undoes nothing."

- **Hard:**
  - "That" points at the measured sentence before it, and "for which"
    means "because of which".
  - "It" in the next sentence is the face subject, three sentences back.
    Its nearest antecedents are now core §11.2 and "every principal".
  - 0.9 rewrote 0.8's "That is F-87's mechanism (core §11.2), which kept
    0.1 and 0.2 from defining a face subject at all". Those last words
    were the antecedent the next sentence's "it" leaned on.
- **Took:** any allow wins across subjects, so a subject in a policy of
  its own undoes the denies of another's. That is why core §11.2
  compiles "every principal" into each principal's own policy. A face
  subject in the far principal's policy undoes nothing.
- **Rewrite:** "Core §11.2 compiles "every principal" into each
  principal's own policy for the same reason: any allow wins across
  subjects. A face subject in the far principal's policy undoes nothing."
- **Changes:** wording only.

### F-333 · hard to read · `link.v1` §2.4 and §2.15, "outside every face whose far principal it is not"

> §2.4: "A subject bound to a principal is selected by the link protocols
> of §2.1's closed list outside every face whose far principal it is not,
> in that list's order."
>
> §2.15, `narrowed_too_far`: "under `allow`, a name the block binds, read
> by its kind, and a link protocol of §2.1's list outside every face whose
> far principal it is not, that no subject answering for that name
> selects."

- **Hard:**
  - A negative relative clause ("whose far principal it is not") inside
    "outside".
  - "It" has two antecedents in each. In §2.4 they are the subject and the
    principal, and only the principal can be a far principal. In §2.15
    they are the name and the link protocol.
  - §2.15's finding is a pair, a name and a link protocol, and its last
    clause belongs to the pair, past a second relative clause.
- **Took:**
  - §2.4: the subject is selected by §2.1's list, in its order, less the
    link protocols of every face whose far principal is another
    principal.
  - §2.15: the finding is a name and a link protocol that §2.4 does not
    keep the name off, when no subject answering for that name selects
    the protocol.
- **Rewrite:**
  - §2.4: "A subject bound to a principal P is selected by §2.1's closed
    list of link protocols, in that list's order, less those of every
    face whose far principal is not P."
  - §2.15: "under `allow`, a name the block binds, read by its kind, and
    a link protocol that §2.4 does not keep that name off: one of §2.1's
    list that no face selects whose far principal is not that name. It is
    the finding when no subject answering for that name selects that link
    protocol."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's generator (`link.compile_faces`,
  with `narrow`) and its check (`link.narrowed_too_far`) read it so.

### F-334 · hard to read · `link.v1` §2.15, "The far principal's policies"

> "A subject naming both kinds adds none. Counted as the far principal's,
> such a subject in a near principal's policy would make that policy one
> the face subject could ride. Every session over the face would then get
> that principal's grants that the far principal's denies do not include,
> its writes to an owner's keys among them (measured, `[Sc: §11]`)."

- **Hard:**
  - A participle whose subject comes after it: "counted" belongs to
    "such a subject".
  - "Ride" is not defined in `v1.md`. Its Appendices A and B, and the
    scenarios' §10, use it for being listed in a policy.
  - "That principal" has two antecedents, the far principal and the near
    one.
  - 0.9 turned 0.8's history, "Under 0.4 such a subject … made that
    policy one the face subject could ride", into this conditional.
- **Took:** if a subject naming both kinds counted as the far principal's,
  a near principal's policy that lists it would be one of the far
  principal's policies. `face_subject_misplaced` would then want the face
  subject listed there. Every session over the face would then get that
  near principal's grants.
- **Rewrite:** "A subject naming both kinds adds none. If it counted as
  the far principal's, a near principal's policy that lists it would be
  one of the far principal's policies, and the face subject would be
  listed in it (`face_subject_misplaced`, below). Every session over the
  face would then get that near principal's grants that the far
  principal's denies do not include, its writes to an owner's keys among
  them (measured, `[Sc: §11]`)."
- **Changes:** wording only.

### F-335 · hard to read · `link.v1` scenarios §11's opening, "binds no name it lists alone"

> "Such a subject binds no name it lists alone, and is not the far
> principal's even when one of its lists names the far principal alone
> (v1.md §2.4, §2.15)."

- **Hard:** "alone" can modify "binds" (it binds none of its names by
  itself) or "lists" (a name it lists alone, the only one in its list).
  The second clause's "names the far principal alone" uses it the second
  way, which pulls the first toward it. 0.9 wrote the sentence from 0.8's
  "0.4 read such a subject as binding each name it lists".
- **Took:** by itself, such a subject binds none of the names it lists:
  v1.md §2.4's "Across its two lists, a subject binds no one alone".
- **Rewrite:** "By itself, such a subject binds none of the names it
  lists. It is not the far principal's even when one of its lists names
  the far principal alone (v1.md §2.4, §2.15)."
- **Changes:** wording only.

### After review-bot on PR #959

Nothing was blocking. The bot's should-fixes and nits:
- **§10's listening** (`alarms_scenarios`). A comment now says why
  `need_ns` holds the reply timeout twice: once for the window's first
  instant, the declaration plus the reply timeout, and once inside the
  watch after it, as the old sum's two reply timeouts were. The loop is
  bounded at its length plus 30 s, and a length not reached by then is a
  harness failure, named `harness:`, never the reader's.
- **A reader for a reading** (`alarms`). The reading of round 86 built an
  `AlarmsReader` with `object.__new__` and set its attributes by hand, so
  an attribute added to `__init__` could break it unseen.
  `AlarmsReader.offline` now builds one through `__init__`. It takes the
  values `window()` reads (the subscription's declaration and
  completeness, the receive path's losses, each owner's instance at the
  start and its token moves, the GETs asked) and stands in for the
  session's watch and subscription. `window()` reads nothing else: the
  watch's lengths and `qos` besides, and the clock when no instant is
  given.
- **Nits.** The watch's length is `bg.watch_after_s(*self.watch)` itself.
  `lease_ns`, which nothing read, is gone. `budget` is imported at module
  level: it imports only the standard library there, so there is no
  cycle.
- **`readings`: 664.** One more case: an offline reader's window under a
  loss, a withdrawal, a complete GET after both (which heals them, the
  window running from it) and an incomplete one (which heals nothing).
  **`just py-conformance`: 3621 of 3621.** `alarms_scenarios --only 10`:
  17 of 17 with zk2py's owners, and 17 of 17 with the owner example's.

### F-336 · contradiction · `desired.v1` §2.7 and §2.16, against `config.v1` §2.12 and §2.18: a `config.v1` owner fed through `desired.v1` that re-mints

> `desired.v1` §2.7: "**A re-mint is not a restart.** A target that mints a
> new instance id in its own process (core §1.5, §8.1) keeps its run: it
> still runs what it applied, and keeps what it acted on, the ids it
> remembers and its report."
>
> `desired.v1` §2.16: "A `config.v1` owner whose document reaches it
> through this profile's reading (a role bound to its author's slice,
> §2.3) acts as §2.7 says. It acts on each version once in a run, whatever
> the outcome."
>
> `config.v1` §2.12: "**A re-mint is a restart.** Core §1.5 lets a running
> process mint a new instance, and a new instance starts from its startup
> values, the revision from 0, nothing pending (above). So an owner
> re-mints while `config.v1` runs only with its device running its startup
> values: nothing pending, and every runtime change of the instance undone
> or persisted, a persisted value being a startup value (§2.13)."
>
> `config.v1` §2.18: "It acts on each version of the document, its
> author's stamp, once in an instance, whatever the outcome." And: "the
> document's next revision is acted on, and so is the same revision by a
> new instance (below)."

- **The contradiction.** Take a `config.v1` owner fed through
  `desired.v1`, converged on a version, that re-mints in its process.
  - By `config.v1`, it first returns its device to its startup values, the
    converged document's values among them, since they were runtime
    changes. Its new instance then acts on the bound version again, once in
    the new instance.
  - By `desired.v1`, it keeps its run. It "still runs what it applied", and
    a delivery of the version it acted on is the same version, never acted
    on again (§2.6).
  - So by `desired.v1` the owner runs its startup values for good, and its
    view's `desired` says the document converged, until the author puts
    another version.
- **Since when.** `config.v1` 0.3 made a re-mint a restart. `desired.v1`
  0.4 made the run its unit (F-192), and its §2.16 has read "once in a
  run" since. `config.v1` §2.18 still reads "once in an instance".
  `desired.v1` §2.16 also says that `config.v1` §2.18 "states this
  profile's rules for one type", so its own sentence and the one it
  delegates to disagree. #935's pass moved neither.
- **Took:** `config.v1`'s rule: for a `config.v1` owner, a re-mint is a
  restart, which begins a new run, so it acts again (`desired.v1` §2.7, "A
  restart acts again"). That keeps the device and the view in step.
- **Fix:** `desired.v1` §2.16, "**A re-mint is a restart** for a
  `config.v1` owner (`config.v1` §2.12): it returns to its startup values
  and begins a new run, so it acts again (§2.7)". Or `config.v1` §2.12
  forbids the re-mint to an owner fed through `desired.v1`.
- **Changes:** an implementation, a `config.v1` owner fed through
  `desired.v1` that re-mints, and what a tool's `config.v1` §5 question
  reads of it. No zk2py verdict: zk2py's config owner converges a document
  bound to it directly, and is never fed through `desired.v1`. The
  reference refuses the re-mint (`config.v1` §2.12), so no run meets
  either reading. No fixture pins a target's re-mint.

### F-337 · hard to read · `alarms.v1` §2.14 step 4, "The establishing GET heals the keys it leaves out": "Otherwise", and "as before"

> "So a key it left out, with nothing of the key arriving after it was
> asked, was neither live when the owner answered nor put since: step 5
> reads it `not_held`. Otherwise a key whose resolve and delete a loss
> took would read `incomplete` for as long as the reader held it. Past the
> tombstone window no GET answers it again, and "is anything firing?" over
> its owner could never read no. A key something of which arrived after
> that GET was asked is not left out: a GET that answers it heals it, as
> before."

- **Hard:**
  - "Otherwise" names no condition. It stands for "without this rule". Its
    nearest condition is the sentence before's, a key left out with
    nothing of it arriving, so it first reads "for any other key", which
    the bullet's last sentence then contradicts. 0.9 wrote it for 0.8's
    "Before 0.5,".
  - "As before" was 0.8's too, beside "Before 0.5". Without that, it
    points at nothing in particular.
- **Took:** without this rule, such a key would read `incomplete` for as
  long as the reader held it. "As before" is step 4's own heal: a GET that
  answers the key heals the loss for it.
- **Rewrite:** "Without this rule, a key whose resolve and delete a loss
  took would read `incomplete` for as long as the reader held it." And:
  "… a GET that answers it heals it, as step 4's first sentence says."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `alarms.judge` reads it so
  (`left_out`, F-136).

### F-338 · hard to read · `alarms.v1` §2.16, "A key's first answer": "Neither splits by its reason"

> "Yes is reported, as above. No is not: no report was made for it to
> clear. Neither splits by its reason, in two closed lists:"

- **Hard:** a name that reads as a pronoun. "Neither" is the name of the
  third answer, unobservable or not asked, which "What is a change to
  report" gives ("between yes, no and neither"). Right after "Yes" and
  "No", it first reads as "neither of them", so the two lists would be of
  yes and no.
- **Took:** an answer that is neither yes nor no, unobservable or not
  asked, splits by its reason.
- **Rewrite:** "An answer of neither, unobservable or not asked, splits by
  its reason, in two closed lists:"
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `alarms.first_neither_list` reads it
  so: each reason of an answer unobservable or not asked is on one of the
  two lists, which the readings family checks.

### F-339 · hard to read · `telemetry.v1` §2.9 step 2, "what it saw between two arrivals is what it saw"

> "A reader's view of them stands on a complete read of the tokens (core
> §8.1, which a subscription's history alone is not), and on nothing lost
> since it. It folds the tokens' moves and the samples in the one order it
> received them, so that what it saw between two arrivals is what it saw:"

- **Hard:** a clause that restates itself. "What it saw … is what it saw"
  says nothing until the reader supplies what it means: the presence the
  reader holds for the time between two arrivals is the presence it
  received in that time, never a later read's. The colon then introduces
  the two established epochs, which are not what "what it saw" is.
- **Took:** token moves and samples are one sequence, ordered by receipt.
  The presence between two arrivals is what the reader received between
  them, and the two items say what that establishes.
- **Rewrite:** "It folds the tokens' moves and the samples into one
  sequence, in the order it received them. So the presence it holds
  between two arrivals is the presence it received between them. From that
  view:"
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's R (`telemetry_scenarios.Reader`)
  stamps the token moves and the samples on one monotonic clock, and reads
  the presence between two arrivals from them (`presence_of`).

### F-340 · hard to read · `telemetry.v1` scenarios, "Conventions", "R pairs": "earlier and later the only token held at each arrival"

> "Its presence is what R saw after its complete read: alone throughout
> when exactly one instance token was held at every instant from before
> the earlier arrival to after the later one's, with no liveliness event
> lost; earlier and later the only token held at each arrival."

- **Hard:** a list run into one sentence, its second item with no verb.
  "Earlier and later" are two presence values, the token held at each of
  the pair's arrivals. They read first as adverbs of "held". The first
  item's "alone throughout" is a label, as §1's Expected lines use it ("I1
  alone throughout"), but nothing marks it as one.
- **Took:** R records one of two presences for a pair. Alone throughout,
  when exactly one instance token was held throughout and no event was
  lost. Or earlier and later: the only token held at the earlier arrival,
  and the only one at the later. v1.md §2.9 then reads them.
- **Rewrite:** "Its presence is what R saw after its complete read, one of
  two:
  - alone throughout: exactly one instance token was held at every
    instant from before the earlier arrival to after the later one's, with
    no liveliness event lost;
  - earlier and later: the only token held at the earlier arrival, and the
    only one held at the later."
- **Changes:** wording only. `telemetry_scenarios.Reader.presence_of`
  records it so: `alone`, then the earlier and the later token.

### F-341 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.3, `two_documents`: "each of them binds the one slice there is not"

> "It sits after `required_unbound`, which reads only whether a binding
> exists and so leaves the kill switch the deployment's whatever the
> requirement names, and before every other problem, alone: each of them
> binds the one slice there is not."

- **Hard:**
  - One sentence holds two placements and a reason for each. The second
    placement, "and before every other problem", comes after a 22-word
    relative clause.
  - "Alone" is the rule that `two_documents` is reported with no other
    problem, which `bindings.json` pins ("two_documents alone, the
    binding's other checks not read"). In the sentence it reads as an
    adverb of "sits".
  - "Each of them binds the one slice there is not": "them" is the other
    problems, and the phrase means each of them is about binding one
    slice, which a role on two documents does not have.
- **Took:** `two_documents` comes after `required_unbound`, so an unbound
  optional role stays the kill switch. It comes before every other
  problem, and is reported alone, since each other problem reads the
  binding of one slice.
- **Rewrite:** "It sits after `required_unbound`, which reads only whether
  a binding exists. So the kill switch stays the deployment's, whatever the
  requirement names. It sits before every other problem, and is reported
  alone: each of the others reads the binding of one slice, and a role on
  two documents has no one slice."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `desired.bind` reports it alone.

### F-342 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.5, "The reference": "which such a target would act on again"

> "**The reference** reads an archive only after a complete read shows its
> author absent, never on a silent GET while its author is present. An
> archive can hold a document its author deleted past its tombstone window
> (§2.8), which such a target would act on again. It can hold one its
> author has since replaced, which it would act on as last-known."

- **Hard:** a term with no antecedent. "Such a target" is one that does
  read an archive on a silent GET while its author is present. The
  sentence before names only the reference, which does not. 0.8 held the
  three in one sentence, a colon making the last two the reason for the
  "never". 0.9's full stop leaves the reader to rebuild both the target and
  the reason. "It" in the third sentence is the archive, two sentences
  after it was named.
- **Took:** the reason the reference waits for absence: a target that
  read an archive on a silent GET could act again on a document its author
  deleted past the window, or act as last-known on one its author has
  since replaced.
- **Rewrite:** "The reference reads an archive only after a complete read
  shows its author absent, never on a silent GET while its author is
  present. An archive can hold a document its author deleted past its
  tombstone window (§2.8), or one its author has since replaced. A target
  that read the archive on a silent GET would act on the first again, and
  on the second as last-known."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's target reads an archive only after a
  complete read shows its author absent (scenarios §10 step 3).

### F-343 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.6 step 3, "equal": "Only a version from an archive is confirmed"

> "- equal: **the same version** (`same_version`), received again by
>   another path or another seed, never acted on again; its author's own
>   sample of a version the target holds from an archive, or holds waiting
>   from an archive while an act runs, **confirms** it (`confirmed`, §2.9).
>   Only a version from an archive is confirmed: any other delivery of a
>   version held waiting, the author's own version included, is the same
>   version;"

- **Hard:**
  - "Any other delivery": other than what? It means any delivery but the
    author's own sample of an archive's version.
  - "The author's own version included" names a version where the
    sentence is about deliveries. It means a version held waiting that
    came from the author, delivered again by the author. Read as written,
    it says the author's own sample is the same version, against the
    sentence before.
  - "Only a version from an archive" is the version held, never the
    delivery. Only "held waiting" is named, so a version held, not
    waiting, that came from the author is left to "equal" at the top.
  - The words are F-184's answer (0.3).
- **Took:** an equal delivery is the same version, but for one: the
  author's own sample of a version held, or held waiting, from an archive,
  which confirms it. A version that came from the author is never
  confirmed, whoever delivers it again.
- **Rewrite:** "- equal: **the same version** (`same_version`), received
  again by another path or another seed, never acted on again. One equal
  delivery is not: the author's own sample of a version the target holds
  from an archive, or holds waiting from an archive while an act runs,
  **confirms** it (`confirmed`, §2.9). A version the target holds, or
  holds waiting, that came from its author is never confirmed: every equal
  delivery of it, its author's included, is the same version;"
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `TargetRole` reads it so, and a
  reading pins the five cases (below).

### F-344 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.6, "Within one id": "Such a case is a value … It is acted on as another id, and the new epoch's next value after it"

> "Two ids for one key are the case the merge leaves to core §4.3. Such a
> case is a value of the author's old epoch still in transit when its new
> epoch's first value has been acted on, and later than every value of the
> old epoch the target acted on. It is acted on as another id, and the new
> epoch's next value after it."

- **Hard:**
  - "Such a case is a value": a case is said to be a value. 0.9 made it a
    sentence of its own, where 0.8's colon introduced the value as what
    the case holds.
  - "It" has two antecedents, the case and the value.
  - The last clause leaves its verb out: "and the new epoch's next value
    [is acted on] after it".
- **Took:** a value of the old epoch, still in transit after the new
  epoch's first value was acted on, and later than every old-epoch value
  the target acted on, is acted on, its id another than the one held. The
  new epoch's next value is acted on after it.
- **Rewrite:** "Two ids for one key are the case the merge leaves to core
  §4.3. In it, a value of the author's old epoch is still in transit when
  the new epoch's first value has been acted on, and it is later than
  every value of the old epoch the target acted on. The target acts on
  that value as another id, then on the new epoch's next value."
- **Changes:** wording only. `order.json` pins the case, and zk2py meets
  it.

### F-345 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.16, "What a delete reverts it to": "named to its startup value"

> "So a delete it acts on reverts each parameter a document it acted on in
> this run named to its startup value: the persisted layer's, else the
> startup file's or the default."

- **Hard:** a garden path. The object of "reverts" holds a relative clause
  with no "that", "a document it acted on in this run named", whose verb
  lands beside "to its startup value". So it first reads "named to its
  startup value". 0.8's commas, around "a refused document's aside", kept
  "named" apart from "to". 0.9 moved that phrase out (F-331's rewrite) and
  left the sentence with neither.
- **Took:** each parameter that a document the owner acted on in this run
  named goes back to its startup value.
- **Rewrite:** "So when it acts on a delete, each parameter named by a
  document it acted on in this run goes back to its startup value: the
  persisted layer's, else the startup file's or the default." That is
  `config.v1` 0.7's own wording ("Each parameter named by a document it
  acted on in this instance goes back to its startup value"), "run" kept
  (F-336).
- **Changes:** wording only.

### F-346 · hard to read · `desired.v1` §2.17, "A requirement unread": "One that declares any is no help"

> "A revision of the author's in hand, named or held, that declares no
> desired resource at all still shows the role no target's, **not
> asked**, `not_a_target`, whatever the requirement names. One that
> declares any is no help, one desired resource included: the requirement
> may name a plain resource beside it, which makes the role no target's,
> and only the requirement says."

- **Hard:** four things left out of one sentence.
  - "Any" is any desired resource.
  - "One desired resource included" means "even when it declares only
    one", and reads first as a member of the revision.
  - "It" in "beside it" is that desired resource.
  - "Only the requirement says" means only the requirement, which the tool
    has not read, could say which resource it names.
- **Took:** with the requirement unread, a revision declaring at least one
  desired resource, even only one, does not settle the role. The
  requirement might name a plain resource of the author's instead, which
  would make the role no target's.
- **Rewrite:** "A revision that declares a desired resource, even only
  one, settles nothing. The requirement may name a plain resource of the
  author's instead, which would make the role no target's. Only the
  requirement, which the tool has not read, says which."
- **Changes:** wording only. zk2py's `desired.take_slice` reads it so
  (round 64's shapes).
